Waratah Minerals Cargo Project — EL5238, Consols and Spur prospects. EPSG:28355. This is a 3D model of drilling, assays, surface geology, faults and interpolants around mineralisation. A conceptual estimate has been run on the mineralisation only. It is not a Mineral Resource or an Ore Reserve under the JORC Code (2012). It is conceptual in nature and run as an experiment for predictive purposes.

Data sourced includes:

  • Waratah significant intercepts from ASX tables (2024 to 22 September 2026), desurveyed as straight holes from the collar dip and azimuth.
  • Historic assays for gold from open DIGS files, matched to MinView collars. 3 historic holes at Consols, 24 at Spur and 4 at Gum Flat. A hole named to that prospect is included. Any other assayed hole within 400 m of a Waratah collar takes that collar's domain (849 composites of 8 m).
  • Ironclad significant intersections from Golden Cross, June 1997, DIGS R00002858 Table 1. Ten reverse-circulation holes. JG139 is the MinView collar, dip −56.5°, azimuth 330°. The other nine collars are digitised from the section inset on that report and tied to JG139. Dip −50°, azimuth 150°. A check on JG154 is about 20 m.
  • NSW 5 m elevation model from the SIX ImageServer NSW_5M_Elevation.
  • Essex Fault is the Figure 1 trace of 22 September 2026, strike about 129°, dip 80° toward 219°.
  • Colthi Fault is the SPD074 piercepoint at 476 m (25 August 2026), east–west, dip 60° south, and it stops 40 m under the DEM.

Grade interpolant is anisotropic inverse distance squared, power 2. The search is one ellipsoid and it shortens as the cutoff rises.

  • Consols (strike / down-dip / thickness) = 70 / 100 / 16 m at 0.5 g/t, 48 / 70 / 12 m at 1 g/t, 32 / 45 / 8 m at 2 g/t. Orientation is east–west, 85° south (22 September 2026).
  • Spur (plunge / east / thickness) = 110 / 40 / 16 m, 70 / 28 / 10 m, 45 / 18 / 7 m. Plunge is 60° south (28 April 2025). There is no top cut.
  • Ironclad (strike / down-dip / thickness) = 60 / 40 / 12 m at 0.5 g/t, 40 / 28 / 8 m at 1 g/t, 25 / 16 / 6 m at 2 g/t. Working orientation is strike 60°, dip 80° toward 150°, across the 1997 drill azimuth.
  • Gum Flat (strike / down-dip / thickness) = 100 / 50 / 12 m at 0.5 g/t, 60 / 30 / 8 m at 1 g/t, 40 / 20 / 6 m at 2 g/t. Working orientation is strike north, dip 15° east. The sonic holes are vertical.

The colour bar runs to 58.47 g/t Au on the Waratah intervals. Historic composites are length-weighted over 8 m, the same support as the Waratah samples, and grades below the cutoff are kept. On a Waratah hole, drilled metres with no reported intercept are carried at 0.05 g/t within 40 m of an ore interval.

  • Conceptual estimate blocks are 14 × 8 × 6 m at Consols, 8 × 12 × 6 m at Spur, 10 × 8 × 6 m at Ironclad and 12 × 10 × 6 m at Gum Flat in that structural frame. A continuous run on the short axis is one prism. Cells above the DEM, and cells within 4 m of it, are excluded. Density is 2.75 t/m³, assigned from Lake Cowal as an analogue. It is not a Cargo measurement. Contained gold is tonnes × grade / 31.1035.

Shells: 0.5 g/t is 32.89 million m³ at Consols, 10.05 million m³ at Spur, 1.04 million m³ at Ironclad and 0.57 million m³ at Gum Flat. 1 g/t is 12.00 million m³, 2.54 million m³, 0.15 million m³ and 0.22 million m³. 2 g/t is 2.66 million m³, 0.31 million m³, 0.01 million m³ and 0.10 million m³.
